title: Seamus Coleman to leave Everton at end of season after 17 years
content:
Seamus Coleman is set to leave Everton at the end of the season, bringing to an end a remarkable 17-year stint at the Merseyside club.

Coleman, 37, confirmed the news in a statement issued on Friday morning, with an emotional farewell expected on Sunday when he plays his final home match as an Everton player against Sunderland.

Everton said a decision has not yet been made on whether he will continue his career elsewhere or take up a role on their coaching staff.

“After more than 17 years at this great football club, I’ve decided this season will be my last as a player here,” he said.

“I want to thank the fans for their unbelievable support. You’ve helped me in more ways than you could imagine. I’ve always tried my best to put Everton first and you all mean the world to me. I live in the city — I see you all daily — and I’ve taken your love of the club back into the dressing room to explain to the lads how much Everton means to the people.

“I also thank my managers, teammates and all the staff at Everton. They’ve seen me happy, sad, angry, emotional, but the greater cause has always been Everton.”

Coleman joined Everton as a £60,000 signing from Sligo Rovers of the League of Ireland in 2009. At his peak, he was one of the Premier League’s best right-backs, earning a place in the team of the season for 2013-14. He was named club captain in 2019, taking over from England international Phil Jagielka, and has made 433 appearances for Everton.

The Republic of Ireland international was widely credited by players and former coaches for helping Everton to remain a top-flight club during years of struggle on and off the pitch. He was seen as a setter of standards, with successive managers keen to keep him around even as his playing time dwindled in recent seasons.

Coleman made just three appearances for Everton this term and will take a break this summer before contemplating his next move.

“After such a big decision, I want to have some time over the summer to focus on what’s next for me and my family,” he added. “My love for Everton is something you all know about – and I’ve got a huge love for Ireland as well.

“The club have been unbelievable with me. They’ve offered me an opportunity to stay on at the club. The manager and staff have been great, and I think with it being such an important decision over my future, I’m going to take a nice, long holiday and look back on what has been an amazing time as an Everton footballer.”

Analysis from Everton Correspondent Patrick Boyland

There is little doubt in my mind that Everton would have been relegated without Coleman’s influence behind the scenes.

“When times got tough, he was the first guy to step forward,” first-team coach and long-time team-mate Leighton Baines told Everton TV in an interview published on Friday.

As a budget signing from Ireland, Coleman defied all the odds to become not only an Everton regular but also one of the best right-backs in the Premier League. Tenacious, athletic and capable of surging forward to help the attack, he was at his pomp in 2013-14 when he named in the Premier League’s Team of the Season.

In recent years, his impact on the pitch his waned. Injuries caught up with him and the last few summers have seen him contemplate whether to extend his time at the club. But managers valued his presence in the dressing room and always wanted him to remain in some capacity.

Those that have worked with him speak fondly about his leadership and the way he reminded players of their responsibilities to the club’s fanbase. Rallying cries were common before key games, particularly those where Everton’s top-flight status was on the line.

“This fella is one of the best people I’ve ever met,” then-manager Frank Lampard said after the 3-2 win over Crystal Palace in 2022 that confirmed Everton’s survival.

What comes next for Coleman will be intriguing. A coaching position at Everton will be available for him if he wishes, and manager David Moyes’ desire will be for him to remain at the club in some capacity. Coleman was pictured next to Moyes, high in the stands at Fulham earlier this season, providing support as the Scot served a touchline ban. But the Everton manager has also noted in recent press conferences that Coleman may not necessarily see his future in coaching. Other options are on the table, including an extension of his playing career elsewhere, with a decision expected this summer after he has taken a break.

Whatever he decides, he has the well wishes of all at Everton.

Sunday’s final home game will be memorable and emotional. It will be a poignant farewell — at least in a playing sense — to an Everton icon.
